context: The homepage order panel could remain visibly stuck on Connecting after the Xaman authorization window was closed. A reset control existed only inside collapsed Wallet details, while the Liquidity Pool already exposed a visible Cancel / restart path and explicit attempt invalidation. The homepage was aligned to the Liquidity Pool lifecycle and the connection behavior was promoted to the project-wide migration standard.
behavior: Connect remains authorization-only and uses XRBCXamanStandard.authorizeAndWarm() from the deliberate browser user gesture.
Read-only backend/XRPL readiness starts in parallel with Xaman authorization.
Browser authorization remains bounded to 180 seconds.
Cancel / restart Xaman is visible in the same top order-panel wallet surface while authorization is active.
The collapsed Wallet details Disconnect control uses the same reset path while authorization is active.
Each connect attempt has explicit identity plus XAMAN_AUTH_GENERATION stale-response protection.
A late response from a cancelled/older attempt cannot adopt or overwrite a newer wallet attempt.
At the three-minute deadline the attempt is invalidated, local authorization state is cleared, bounded SDK logout is attempted, and the UI returns to a deliberate Connect action.
No automatic replacement authorization, automatic reconnect loop, or transaction payload is created.
Existing pending/ambiguous transaction request records remain protected across wallet cancellation/reset.

project_connection_standard.browser_connect: Invoke XRBCXamanStandard.authorizeAndWarm() immediately from the deliberate Connect user gesture; start read-only backend/XRPL readiness in parallel.
project_connection_standard.xapp_connect: When sdk.runtime.xapp is true, use the account supplied by the Xaman xApp runtime; do not invoke unsupported browser OAuth/authorization from inside the xApp.
project_connection_standard.connection_vs_signing: Connection establishes public account/signing authorization only. It must not create a ledger-changing transaction.
project_connection_standard.one_active_attempt: Keep a per-attempt identity/generation guard so obsolete responses cannot become current.
project_connection_standard.visible_cancel_restart: Expose Cancel / restart in the same visible connection surface while browser authorization is active.
project_connection_standard.timeout_cleanup: Invalidate the attempt, clear local signing authorization, perform bounded SDK logout, and return to an explicit Connect action.
project_connection_standard.no_auto_retry: Timers/countdowns may explain or terminate a current attempt; they must never create a replacement authorization or transaction payload.
project_connection_standard.remembered_account_rule: A remembered public XRPL address is display/read state only and is not proof of current Xaman signing readiness.
project_connection_standard.pending_request_rule: Disconnect/reset must not silently delete or release an already-created or ambiguous signing-request guard.
project_connection_standard.transaction_rule: Ledger writes stay separate: exactly one Xaman payload per deliberate final intent, challenge/intent binding, bounded expiry, validated tesSUCCESS, signer/account equality, and critical-field comparison.

manual_checks: Close a browser authorization window and verify Cancel / restart remains immediately usable.
Cancel/reset then start a second authorization; a late result from the first must not replace the second.
Allow one attempt to reach 180 seconds and verify safe reset with no transaction request.

invariants: Wallet connection is authorization only; no transaction is created merely to connect.
No Xaman transaction payload during backend warm-up.
Exactly one Xaman payload per deliberate final transaction intent.
Ambiguous payload creation is reconciled and never auto-replaced.
Final transaction success requires validated XRPL evidence, tesSUCCESS, signer/account equality, and critical-field comparison.
